sections.overview: The Greater Scaup is a circumpolar diving duck that breeds in northern wetlands and winters widely along coasts. Like the Common Pochard (Aythya ferina), it belongs to Aythya. Compared with that relative, it winters more often on marine shores.
sections.identification: The male is black and white with a rounded head; females are brown, and both sexes have pale blue bills.
sections.habitat: It nests beside shallow Arctic and subarctic lakes, while wintering birds gather on bays, estuaries and sheltered coastal waters.
sections.diet: It dives for molluscs, crustaceans and aquatic insects, also taking aquatic plants and seeds, especially in inland waters.
sections.behavior: Outside breeding, it forms large rafts and feeds by diving; coastal winter flocks may be far offshore.
sections.reproduction: The female builds a down-lined ground nest near water, incubates the eggs and leads the downy, mobile ducklings.
sections.ecology: Its diving for benthic prey connects shallow-lake and marine food webs, with habitat use shifting between seasons.
sections.conservation: Global and regional assessments report declines in some populations, although monitoring remains uneven across its vast range.
